opportunities.title: auth refresh endpoint issues tokens without verifying the requester
opportunities.summary: ## Bug `POST /api/auth/refresh` currently issues a fresh access token without checking the requester at all. The service also signs that token for the hard-coded subject `usr_existing` with role `client`, so even an authenticated caller does not get a token for their own subject and role. ## Expected fix Protect the refresh route with the existing bearer-token auth middleware, pass the verified user payload into the refresh service, and sign the refreshed token for that authenticated subject and role. Add route-level tests for unauthenticated rejection and authenticated subject preservation. ## Scope This issue is limited to the auth refresh route/service behavior for `/api/auth/refresh` and focused API tests. This issue is limited only to the creator of this issue. This means that only the issue author can attempt to solve this issue. If you would like to work on it, please create another issue with the same contents and refer to issue #743 for more information. References #743.

opportunities.title: [Bounty: $70] Allow LilySdk.withConfig overrides to clear inherited credentials
opportunities.summary: **Context** `LilySdk.withConfig(overrides)` in `src/sdk.ts` merges credentials from the parent config whenever the override does not supply its own: `...(overrides.apiKey !== undefined ? { apiKey: overrides.apiKey } : this.config.apiKey !== undefined ? { apiKey: this.config.apiKey } : {})`. There is no way to create a tenant-scoped or public child that removes an inherited `apiKey` or `authToken`. A parent configured with a global key therefore leaks it into every child, even when the child should authenticate differently or anonymously, and users work around it by constructing a fresh `LilySdk` instead of using `withConfig`. **Proposed Change** Add an explicit opt-out convention (e.g. accept `apiKey: null` or an `{ apiKey: undefined }` sentinel documented in the type) so an override can clear an inherited credential, and document the semantics in the `withConfig` JSDoc and README. **Acceptance Criteria** - A child created with the clearing sentinel sends neither `x-api-key` nor `Authorization`. - Credentials still inherit when no override is given. - Behavior is covered by tests in `tests/sdk-with-config.test.ts` and documented. **Suggested Label** (enhancement) **ETA:** 24 hours

opportunities.title: [Add] TON: gasless transfers via W5 relayer — pay fees in USDT (revenue line) [TON / Gasless]
opportunities.summary: **What:** Gasless TON transfers — users pay fees in the token they're sending (USDT etc.) instead of needing native TON. **This is a revenue line, not just UX:** the user signs a batch containing their transfer plus a fee payment to our relayer; the relayer (VultiServer is the natural host) broadcasts, pays the native gas, and keeps the in-token fee. Phantom charges ~1.5% for the equivalent on Solana; Tonkeeper monetizes via Battery. **Why users expect it:** "Can't send my $2,000 USDT because I have no TON" is the top wallet-switching complaint in the TON ecosystem; Tonkeeper and Telegram Wallet both ship it. **How it works with our vaults:** the relayer is broadcast-side only — it never joins the key ceremony. Fast and secure vaults sign the same W5 batch; the relayer can't alter it (signature covers the batch), worst case it declines to broadcast. Non-custodial throughout. **Depends on:** W5 wallet contract support (#2181's W5 item) — gasless is a W5 feature. Revenue/parity item under epic #2181.

opportunities.title: parse_duration drops the days (d) unit
opportunities.summary: ## Bug `parse_duration` silently drops the **days** (`d`) unit. The README lists `d` as a supported unit, but the parser ignores it and returns a wrong (too-small) result instead of raising or counting it. ### Reproduction ```python from duration_utils import parse_duration parse_duration("1d") # -> 0 (expected 86400) parse_duration("2d4h") # -> 14400 (expected 187200) ``` ### Expected `d` should be counted as 86400 seconds, so `parse_duration("1d") == 86400` and `parse_duration("2d4h") == 187200`. ### Notes The `d` character is already accepted by the token regex, so malformed-input detection still passes — the value is just never added. A fix should add the `d` unit and cover it with tests. /bounty $50
